newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola unveils new Diet Coke ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola unveils new Diet Coke ad campaign.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co on Tuesday announced a new television ad campaign for Diet Coke, aimed partly at reversing a dip in the leading low-calorie soft drink's U.S. market share.
The campaign, consisting of eight commercials and the slogan "You Are What You Drink" will run for six months in the United States beginning next Monday.
A worldwide rollout was set for later in the month, including overseas markets where the soft drink is known as Coca-Cola Light.

The ads, all of them humorous, depart from the previous "Just For The...Of It" Diet Coke campaign by building on a new personal confidence theme that Coke executives hope will draw new consumers to the brand.
"Today's consumer mindset is about looking and feeling your best, whatever one perceives that to be," Coke marketing chief Sergio Zyman said in a statement.
"This latest round of very different ads is designed to capture the holistic attitude of young adults who believe that being confident is what is most appealing."
Diet Coke was the No. 3 soft drink in the United States in terms of overall sales last year, finishing behind Coke Classic and Pepsi-Cola and even managing to eke out a 2.3 percent rise in volume.

But according to the trade journal Beverage Digest, colas lost out generally to non-colas such as Sprite, Dr. Pepper and Mountain Dew. As a result, Diet Coke's U.S. market share for all soft-drink brands slipped 0.1 percent to 8.7 percent.
Reversing that drop is important for Coca-Cola, which is on a aggressive campaign to raise its share of the entire U.S. soft drink market to 50 percent by the end of the decade.
The U.S. market share stood at 43.1 percent in 1996.
In a bid to boost sales, Coca-Cola launched its first repackaging of Diet Coke in three years in February.

Coca-Cola released four of the eight new ads for critical review on Tuesday. Three concentrate on women as consumers. In one, set on a snowy Alaskan street corner, two men rave about the looks of passing women who are hidden beneath heavy coats and hats, but who carry Diet Coke bottles.
The theme is reversed by another ad in which a roomful of female office workers ogle a scruffy young delivery boy as he leans his manly frame back to empty a bottle of Diet Coke.
A third ad uses the Snow White theme of a wicked witch whose lack of confidence will never convince the mirror that she is the fairest one of all, even if she drinks Diet Coke.
Coke spokesman Bob Bertini said sexual attraction has nothing to do with the campaign's underlying message.
"It's the confidence that you have. It's really about confidence and it's very tongue in cheek," he said.
